text: {"distance_m": 3.5, "reasoning_short": "This is an estimate from typical small-spot detection data, not an exact value. Detecting a small spot is a contrast-times-area task (Ricco's law), not a resolution task like reading an eye chart. Under normal indoor light, a fully black dot on a light background can be noticed at roughly 0.5 arcmin. At 30% contrast it needs about 1/0.3 times the area, so about 1/sqrt(0.3) times the diameter. That gives roughly 0.9 to 1 arcmin. A 1 mm spot at 1 arcmin (0.00029 rad) is seen from about 1 mm / 0.00029 ≈ 3.4 m, and at 0.9 arcmin from about 3.8 m. So the spot stops being visible at roughly 3.5 m."}
